Definition: from G243; from elsewhere:--some other way.
BiblicalUsage: Once, in the parable of the sheepfold: He that entereth not by the door into the sheepfold, but climbeth up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber. The word is the other way in, the climb over the wall instead of the walk through the door.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for some other way carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the warning, that there is one door and every other way in is a thief's way.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
